# Each structural operation is undone by its inverse, rebased onto HEAD:
# changes made since the reverted commit are kept.

env GIT_EDITOR=true
sesam-repo admin s.txt
exec sesam hook install

exec sesam tell --user bob --recipient $BOB_PUBKEY --group dev
cp $TMPDIR/s.txt s
exec sesam add s --group dev
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'setup'

# Groups: the reverted commit added ops, a later one added qa. Only ops goes.
exec sesam user change-groups --user bob --group dev --group ops
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'bob joins ops'
exec sesam user change-groups --user bob --group dev --group ops --group qa
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'bob joins qa'

exec sesam revert HEAD~1
stdout '^~ user bob groups: dev, qa$'
exec git revert --continue
exec sesam user list --json
stdout '"qa"'
! stdout '"ops"'

# An access change goes back; admin-only counts as a change too.
exec sesam add s --group admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'admin-only s'
exec sesam revert HEAD
stdout '^~ secret s access: dev$'
exec git revert --continue
exec sesam --identity $BOB_KEY reveal s

# A secret bob cannot read stays removed when he reverts its removal.
cp $TMPDIR/s.txt hidden
exec sesam add hidden --group admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'add hidden'
exec sesam rm hidden
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'remove hidden'
exec sesam --identity $BOB_KEY revert HEAD
stdout 'skipped secret.remove hidden: you cannot read it, so it cannot come back'
stderr 'nothing to revert'

# A removed secret comes back with its access list and its content.
exec sesam rm s
rm s
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'remove s'
exec sesam revert HEAD
stdout '^\+ secret s \(access: dev\)$'
exec git revert --continue
cmp s $TMPDIR/s.txt
exec sesam --identity $BOB_KEY verify --all
stderr 'Integrity: ok'

# A move goes back to the old path.
exec sesam mv s s2
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'move s'
exec sesam revert HEAD
stdout '^~ secret s2 -> s$'
exec git revert --continue
exec sesam ls --json
stdout '"revealed_path": "s"'
! stdout 's2'
cmp s $TMPDIR/s.txt

# A rename goes back to the old name.
exec sesam user rename bob robert
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'rename bob'
exec sesam revert HEAD
stdout '^~ user robert -> bob$'
exec git revert --continue
exec sesam user list
stdout bob
! stdout robert

# A rotated signing key is never rolled back; with nothing else in the commit
# there is nothing to revert, and git is left as it was.
exec sesam user regen-sign-key --user bob
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'rotate bob'
exec sesam revert HEAD
stdout 'skipped user.regenerate_sign_key bob: a signing key is never rolled back'
stderr 'nothing to revert'
exec git status --porcelain
! stdout .
! exists .git/REVERT_HEAD

# Only an admin may kill, so bob cannot revert a tell; nothing is left behind.
exec sesam tell --user carol --recipient $CAROL_PUBKEY --group dev
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'tell carol'
! exec sesam --identity $BOB_KEY revert HEAD
stderr 'admin'
exec git status --porcelain
! stdout .
! exists .git/REVERT_HEAD

# Merge commits are refused: revert what they brought in instead.
exec git checkout -b topic
cp $TMPDIR/s.txt plain.txt
exec git add -f plain.txt
exec git commit -m 'plain file'
exec git checkout master
exec git merge --no-ff -m 'merge topic' topic
! exec sesam revert HEAD
stderr 'the commit is a merge'

-- s.txt --
secret=1
